title: Rajab and Sha'ban
hook: the months of preparation before Ramadan

segments.voice: Yesterday, Rabi' al-Awwal: a mawlid for some, an ordinary month for others, and love for him on both sides. Today, the two months before the big one.

'A'ishah lived close enough to notice his habits, including the shape of his fasting through the year. In Sahih al-Bukhari she says, in paraphrase: I never saw him fast a complete month except Ramadan, and I never saw him fast more in any month than in Sha'ban. So the month right before Ramadan wasn't a pause, a last chance to eat before the fast. It was the month he fasted most of all, outside Ramadan itself.
screen: `WHAT 'A'ISHAH NOTICED.` → `MOST OF ALL IN SHA'BAN.` → `THE ROAD UP TO THE DOOR.`

segments.voice: First, Rajab. You met it a few days ago, the sacred month that stands alone between Jumada and Sha'ban, and back in year two as well. So the run-up to Ramadan begins inside sacred time, with the verse still ringing: wrong not yourselves in them. Second, Sha'ban, and why. In a report kept by al-Nasa'i, Usamah ibn Zayd asks the Prophet: I don't see you fast in any month the way you fast in Sha'ban. His answer, in paraphrase: it's a month people neglect, between Rajab and Ramadan, and a month in which deeds are lifted up to the Lord of the worlds, and I love for my deeds to be lifted up while I'm fasting. Squeezed between a sacred month and the month of the fast, it's easy to skip. He didn't. Third, catching up. 'A'ishah says in al-Bukhari that when she owed fasts from the last Ramadan, she would make them up in Sha'ban. So it's also the month for settling accounts. Fourth, the middle of Sha'ban. Some communities keep that night with extra prayer, remembering the dead and asking forgiveness. Other scholars hold that the reports about that night are weak, and they don't set it apart. Both sides speak from the reports as they read them. Put together, it's a runner's warmup. Nobody wakes up and races. Rajab and Sha'ban are the stretching: a little fasting, a little extra prayer, old debts cleared, so when Ramadan opens, the habits are already moving.
screen: `RAJAB: SACRED TIME FIRST.` · `SHA'BAN: THE MONTH PEOPLE NEGLECT.` · `CATCHING UP ON OLD FASTS.` · `A WARMUP, NOT A PAUSE.`

segments.voice: Whether or not you'll fast in Ramadan, pick one small habit you'd like to be steady by then: waking a little earlier, reading a page a day, a few minutes of quiet. Picture doing it tomorrow, at the exact time and place, and the day after; a warmup is small on purpose. If you pray, you can ask for help keeping it.
Rajab and Sha'ban. The two months before Ramadan: a sacred month, then the month the Prophet fasted most outside Ramadan, a time people neglect. Today's word.
Your line: getting ready. A warmup, not a pause. Day one thousand three hundred fifty-seven, done.

howItsDone: Some Muslims add voluntary fasts in Sha'ban, following 'A'ishah's report in al-Bukhari that the Prophet fasted most in that month outside Ramadan, and make up missed Ramadan fasts before the next one begins; some communities also keep the night of the middle of Sha'ban with extra prayer, while others don't set it apart.

chat.says: Is Sha'ban just a normal month before Ramadan starts?
options: Not quite. The Prophet fasted more in Sha'ban than any month but Ramadan.
Yes. It's for eating well and resting up before the long fast begins.
No. It's a second required fast, a full month just like Ramadan.
chat.meaning: 'A'ishah said she never saw him fast more in any month than Sha'ban, outside Ramadan. He called it a month people neglect.
